content: An allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before starting rifapentine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other rifamycins (such as rifampin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Avoid alcohol consumption, as it may increase the risk of liver disease. Rifapentine may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary. If taken during the last few weeks of pregnancy, there is an increased risk of bleeding in both the mother and the infant. Notify your doctor immediately if you observe any bleeding in your newborn. It is not known whether rifapentine passes into breast milk, but similar drugs are known to do so. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Rifapentine can accelerate the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods (e.g., pills, patches, or rings), which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Rifapentine may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., folate and vitamin B12 levels), potentially causing inaccurate test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory Monitoring: While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., sputum tests, liver function tests, bilirubin levels, complete blood counts) should be conducted. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose and remember on the same day, take it as soon as you remember. If you remember the next day or later, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is used in combination with other medications to treat active tuberculosis (TB) of the lungs. It may also be used with another medication (isoniazid) to prevent active TB infections in individuals infected with the bacteria (e.g., those with a positive TB skin test). Rifapentine is classified as a rifamycin antibiotic. This antibiotic treats bacterial infections only and will not work for viral infections (e.g., common cold, flu). How to Use: Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting rifapentine and each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally with food as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice weekly. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, take it on the same day(s) of the week and at the same time each day. Continue taking this medication (and other TB medications) for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms disappear. Side Effects: Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or headache. This medication may cause urine, sweat, saliva, or tears to turn reddish, which is harmless and will resolve once the medication is stopped. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects.
